Gk2QTkskOdw.d1: The Vienna U-Bahn is a 5-line rapid transit system serving the Austrian capital. It opened in 1976 with the U4 and has since grown to a size of 83 kilometers. With an annual ridership of 404 million people. Only the U1 and U3 were built as regular metro lines. The others all use at least some part of Vienna’s historic Stadtbahn system, or originally built to accommodate trams underground. There is currently a 5th line under construction, said to take up the downtown part of the line U2, and also be completely automatic. The section currently operated by U2 has already been retrofitted with platform screen doors, and the new trains that will be used on the line are also in operation. The line is supposed to open next year and will add some much-needed connections to the network. It's very well integrated with the rest of the transit system, and the fare system is based on zones. The U-Bahn overall is a very intuitive and efficient metro system. I recommend you use it if you find yourself in Vienna, and as always, enjoy the video :)

_pyPDf4JjFE.d1: (4K, 2026, Right-Hand Side) A beautiful winter train ride in the snow along scenic Line 1, the Holmenkollen Line, on the Oslo T-Bane (Metro), from Ris to Frognerseteren. I did not plan in advance to record this, nor was I equipped to do so, and as such this is a midweek bonus surprise video, and quite informal! I simply recorded it holding my GoPro HERO 12 camera in my hand. The plan was to ride to the top of of the line at Frognerseteren, and walk back down to Holmenkollen by the famous Holmenkollbakken Ski Jump (which can be seen here from the train), before capturing the train down again. However, it was far too icy to walk, and packed with skiers and sledders enjoying the weather on a Sunday afternoon! I knew that this metro line is supposedly considered the most scenic metro line in the world, and I thought it was so beautiful in the snow that I decided to take out my camera, and film what I could, starting from the station at Ris. I certainly plan to go back and video the line in full properly in the future! Also watch our for the pizzeria on the platform at Vettakollen, and all the sledders and skiers who join the train to ride back up to the top of the forested hill again at Midstuen!

8_Vg7XExdIk.d1: The Metro in Sofia Bulgaria is one of the many central-European metro systems built in the late 20th century. Like many soviet metro systems built in neighbouring countries the stations are often large and well decorated making each station unique and easy to identify. M3 was built much later than the other ones which means it’s more modern however they still kept the stations extravagant. It is also one of the only cities in the world to use rope platform barriers. They are a cheaper alternative to platform screen doors and heavily increase safety on the system. The rolling stock consists mainly of Russian Metrowagonmash trains but the newest trains on M3 were built by Siemens. The oldest trains have been gradually refurbished but some still remain in original condition making Sofia the only city in the EU to still operate unrefurbished Metrowagonmash trains from the Soviet Union era. I felt the vibe of this Metro system to be quite unique, and I recommend anyone who finds themselves in Sofia to use it since it is surprisingly extensive and useful. Enjoy the video :)

Because of its past the line is very steep and had to be built with rubber tyred trains. These trains are more efficient than steel wheeled ones because they have better traction so they can climb slopes faster and easier. It is also fully automatic with platform screen doors at every station making it very safe.
